# Inverse and Internal Rendering

Also called: GS-IR, Inner 3D Gaussian Splatting, InnerGS

## Overview
Inverse and Internal Rendering extends 3D Gaussian Splatting beyond surface reconstruction to estimate physical scene properties (lighting, material) from unknown illumination [14852-gs-ir.md] and to reconstruct internal volumetric structures from sparse, pose-free data [15745-inner-3d-gaussian-splatting.md]. Unlike standard 3DGS which optimizes for camera-visible surfaces, this family addresses occluded interiors and implicit volumetric density, solving the failure of projection-based methods on non-surface data and the lack of native normal/material attributes in standard splatting.

## Shared principles
The family shares the core 3D Gaussian representation defined by a mean position $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and a covariance matrix $\Sigma$. The Gaussian function is defined as [S1]:
$$
g(x|\mu, \Sigma) = e^{-\frac{1}{2} (x-\mu)^T \Sigma^{-1} (x-\mu)}
$$
where $\Sigma$ is decomposed into rotation $R$ and scale $S$ such that $\Sigma = RSS^\top R^\top$ [15745-inner-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].

Rendering follows the standard front-to-back alpha compositing equation for a pixel $(u, v)$ [15745-inner-3d-gaussian-splatting.md]:
$$
I(u, v) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i(u, v)\alpha_i c_i \prod_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - p_j(u, v)\alpha_j)
$$
where $p_i(u, v)$ is the 2D density of the $i$-th Gaussian projected onto the image plane, $\alpha_i$ is opacity, and $c_i$ is color derived from Spherical Harmonics (SH) coefficients [14852-gs-ir.md][15745-inner-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].

## Subtopics

### [GS-IR](14852-gs-ir.md)
An inverse rendering approach that estimates scene geometry, surface material (Albedo, Metallic, Roughness), and environment illumination from multi-view images under unknown lighting. It differs from NeRF-based inverse methods by using forward mapping splatting for real-time efficiency and addresses the lack of native normals in 3DGS via depth-derivation regularization. It uses a three-stage optimization: geometry/normal, occlusion baking, and material/illumination.

### [Inner 3D Gaussian Splatting](15745-inner-3d-gaussian-splatting.md)
A framework for direct volumetric inference from sparse, pose-free sliced data (e.g., CT/MRI). It solves the problem of empty interiors in standard 3DGS by using **Conditional Splatting**, which adapts bounding boxes per slice based on conditional Gaussians, unlike sibling methods that project identical bounding boxes. It combines conditional 2D Gaussians with a marginal 1D Gaussian to model continuous volumetric density without explicit camera projection matrices.

### GS-IR (Gaussian Splatting for Internal Rendering)
A plane-based internal rendering framework that replaces exterior-view supervision with cross-sectional supervision sampled from a volume to reconstruct internal volumetric structure [S1].
*   **Definition:** GS-IR focuses optimization gradients on interior Gaussians to supervise occluded internal regions, unlike conventional 3DGS which constrains camera-visible surfaces [S1].
*   **Steps:** Virtual cameras define slicing planes within the volume [S1]. A binary mask selects the Gaussian subset whose centers lie within the plane thickness [S1]. The selected subset is rendered using the original Gaussian rasterizer [S1]. Optimization is performed against ground-truth cross-sections generated through trilinear resampling [S1]. Distance-aware soft weighting is applied to continuously attenuate Gaussian opacity as the distance from the Gaussian to the plane increases [S1].
*   **Parameters:** Plane thickness defines the spatial extent for Gaussian selection [S1].
*   **Performance:** GS-IR improves PSNR by up to 21.52 dB and SSIM by up to 0.54 on KiTS23 CT and IXI MRI datasets [S1].
*   **Usage:** Applied to 3DGS, 2DGS, and Mip-Splatting without modifying their rasterizers [S1].

## Background
The concept of inverse rendering with Gaussians was introduced by Choishroy et al. in 2026, proposing GS-IR to handle internal view synthesis from volumetric data [S1]. The specific "Inner 3D Gaussian Splatting" (InnerGS) framework and its conditional splatting mechanism are described in unofficial notes [15745-inner-3d-gaussian-splatting.md]. The family builds on [3D Gaussian Splatting Implementation Details](9128-3d-gaussian-splatting-implementation-details.md).
